To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

ecto-ATPhydrolysis is the major pathway for energy metabolism in normal neutrophils, and that in chronic granulocyticleukaemia the ectoenzyme is patchy in distribution and that ecto-ADPhydrolysis and 5′nucleotidasedeposition are heterogeneous between cells.

the ectoenzymes Mg2+-dependent adenosine triphosphatase (ATPase), adenosine diphosphatase (ADPase) and 5′ nucleotidase were localized on the plasma membrane of normal human neutrophils, and that the localization of the enzymes in the plasma membranes of neutrophils from patients with chronic myeloid leukaemia varied from that seen in normal cells.

the ectoenzymes Mg2+-dependent adenosine triphosphatase (ATPase), adenosine diphosphatase (ADPase) and 5′ nucleotidase are localized to the plasma membranes of human neutrophils and that in leukaemic granulocytes these ectoenzymes are often absent or present in an abnormal distribution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the structure and function of the neutrophilic granulocyte in normal subjects and in patients with chronic granular leukaemia.
the study of the distribution of nucleoside triphosphatases in normal human neutrophilic granulocytes and in cells from patients with chronic myeloid leukaemia.
the localization of nucleosidase phosphatases in the plasma membranes and granules of normal and leukaemic human polymorphonuclear leukocytes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ectoenzyme distribution of ATPase and 5’-nucleotidae was normal in most chronic granulocyticleukaemia cells, but ADPase was abnormal, being absent from many cells and present in specific granule and background cytoplasm in others.
the enzyme heterogeneity observed in the chronic granulocyticleukaemic cells is not a reflection of the degree of cell maturity.
the ecto-nucleotide phosphatase activities in human granulocytes are altered in chronic granulocyticleukaemia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in normal human neutrophils ecto-ATPAse, ADPase, and 5′nucleotidases were predominantly localized on the plasma membrane and in specific granules.
in normal human neutrophils ecto-ATPAse, ADPase, and 5′nucleotidases are present on the plasma membrane.
ecto-ATPAse and 5′ - nucleotidase were localized in the plasma membrane and ADPase was also present as a cytoplasmic enzyme in the specific granules.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there is considerable heterogeneity in enzyme distribution in leukaemic granulocytes and that the distribution pattern of the various enzymes in leukaemic cells may be quite different from that in normal granulocytes.

the ectoenzymes ATPase, ADPage, and 5′ nucleotidase are localized to the outer surface (ecto) of the plasma membrane in normal human neutrophils but are heterogeneously localized to both the plasma membrane and the granules of the abnormal neutrophils from patients with CML.
the distribution of ecto-ATPsase and ADPase is altered in chronic granulocyticleukaemia.
